text:
Sam: Quick experiment proposal — separate prefill and decode batchers in a prod-like canary to reduce tail spikes. Posting config + results plan here, want quick sanity checks before I spin up the canary.

Maria: Sounds good. What are the token budget targets?

Sam: Thinking: prefill batch token target = 1024 (maximize kernel throughput), decode token target = 64 (favor low latency). Queue policy: prefill uses size-first (min-batch-size 8), decode uses time-window (10ms) to avoid waiting on long prompts.

Alex: Two quick calls outs: 1) KV cache warmup might regress for short-decode-heavy workloads if decode batches don't include prefill tokens. 2) kernel selection fallback behavior needs to be deterministic per-variant when we split.

Sam: Agreed. Measured a tiny KV hit drop in a micro-canary (details below). Also noticed a kernel fallback that increased p95 on one GPU class.

Jen: Can you paste the profiling snippet? Even a short one helps.

Sam: Sure — here's sample profiler output from the micro-canary (trimmed):
```
model: gpt-medium-q4
workload: 70% short chats, 30% long prefill
prefill: p50=55ms p95=120ms p99=320ms
decode: p50=12ms p95=88ms p99=240ms
KV_hit: baseline 0.90 -> split 0.84
kernel_choices: [fast-attn-fp16, attn-quant-int8 (fallback 3x)]
GPU_occupancy: baseline 72% -> split 75%
```

Maria: KV_hit -6% is expected. How much does that translate to token-op cost?

Sam: Rough calc: extra KV misses ~0.6ms/token on average for this model, so cost up ~4% token-time. But p95 improved because decode latency reduced jitter. Net is positive for tail-sensitive apps.

Kevin: Important: perf-ci flagged a regression when kernel selection switched to the quantized attention kernel on older drivers (12GB cards). p95 token latency +12% in one run. We need kernel pin or guard.

Alex: We can pin kernel subsets per model-variant in the runtime config. Also add a quick runtime check: if fallback count > 2/min, revert to combined-batcher mode for that shard.

Jen: Also propose a phase-aware scheduler tweak: allow prefill batches to donate leftover token budget to decode during low prefill load, but enforce an absolute CPU/GPU usage cap so we don't starve long-running prefill kernels. Pseudoconfig: 
```json
{"phase_governor": {"donation_enabled": true, "donation_window_ms": 50, "max_gpu_pct": 0.85}}
```

Sam: Plan for canary: A/B 50/50 traffic for 6 hours with these changes: split-batcher + phase_governor + kernel-pin on older GPU classes + decode-time-window. Track: p50/p95/p99 (prefill/decode separate), KV_hit, kernel_fallback_count, GPU_occupancy, retry/error rates.

Maria: I'll add dashboards and alerts. Also create a synthetic replay that matches 70/30 split and some 200-token prefill tails.

Sam: PR will include fallback to combined-batcher if GPU pressure > 85% OR fallback_count > 5/min. Jen will open the PR for the scheduler tweak.

Jen: On it. Will add unit tests for donation logic and an integration test that simulates KV_miss spikes.

perf-ci-bot: perf-ci: baseline (last 24h) p95_overall=120ms; canary_run_01 p95_overall=106ms; KV_hit=0.84; kernel_fallbacks=3; gpu_occupancy=76%

Alex: Nice. Any regression seen in error rates?

Sam: No error spike seen in run_01, but we saw short decoder starvation during a 5% QPS burst in run_02 — observed ~1.6s tail events on decode-only paths. Root cause: decode queue time-window + immediate prefill donation raced with kernel handoff, causing kv-cache miss storms.

Maria: Suggest adding a tiny decode-prefetch: when a decode batch is formed, and model has KV for that session, prefetch top-k KV pages async. Should reduce misses for short bursts.

Kevin: Sounds reasonable. Also make the kernel-pin list editable via runtime flags so we don't need a deploy for quick rollbacks.

Sam: Final canary summary after 6h (posting numbers):
- p50 overall: baseline 36ms -> canary 34ms
- p95 overall: baseline 120ms -> canary 106ms (improved)
- p99 overall: baseline 420ms -> canary 350ms (improved)
- KV_hit: baseline 0.90 -> canary 0.84 (drop)
- GPU_occupancy: baseline 72% -> canary 77% (up)
- kernel_fallback_count: 3 -> 1 after pinning
- observed decoder-starvation events: 2 (1.2% of requests) -> fixed by decode-prefetch in run_03

Maria: Thanks — I'll mark dashboards green and set alert thresholds: p95 delta > 15ms and KV_hit < 0.75.

Sam: Next steps: roll 10% more traffic with donation_enabled=true + decode-prefetch, monitor for 12h. If p95 stays improved and KV_hit stabilizes above 0.80, proceed to full roll.

Alex: Thx everyone. Leave notes in the PR for kernel-pin rationale.

Jen: PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/3729 (scheduler + donation + tests).

Sam: Will link canary job logs when the 12h run finishes. :thumbsup:
